svg.font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: EEG brain waves: delta, theta, alpha, beta and gamma
svg.desc: One second of each EEG frequency band drawn on the same time scale, with relative amplitudes typical of a scalp recording. Delta, 0.5 to under 4 Hz, is slow and large and is seen in deep sleep. Theta, 4 to under 8 Hz, appears in drowsiness and light sleep. Alpha, 8 to 13 Hz, is the rhythm of the relaxed, awake brain with the eyes closed, strongest over the back of the head. Beta, 14 to 30 Hz, is low and fast and goes with alertness. Gamma, over 30 Hz, is faster still and small. A scale bar shows one second.
svg.text: EEG frequency bands, one second each
Deep sleep; abnormal if prominent in an awake adult
Drowsiness and light sleep; normal in children
Awake and relaxed, eyes closed; over the back of the head
Alert, concentrating; increased by some sedative drugs
Fast activity studied in research; hard to separate from muscle
